Here is the translation of the given ancient Greek text to English:

Then again, the lord of men, Agamemnon, addressed him:
“I rejoice, Laertiades, hearing your words:
For you have judged and recounted everything according to fate.
These things I wish to swear, and my heart urges me,
I will not perjure myself before the divine. But let Achilles
remain there, eager though he be for Ares:
Let all others remain, gathered together, so that the gifts
may come from the tent and we may cut the trustworthy oaths.
To you yourself I command and order this:
Choosing the best young men of the Panachaeans,
bring the gifts from my ship, as many as we promised
to give to Achilles yesterday, and lead the women.
Let Talthybius quickly prepare a boar throughout the wide army of the Achaeans
to cut for Zeus and Helios.”

This passage is from Homer's *Iliad*, specifically from Book 19, lines 184-197. It depicts Agamemnon's response to Odysseus' advice and his instructions for the reconciliation with Achilles.
